label: CRS112-8P-4S-IN
description: Eight-port Gigabit PoE switch with 802.3af/at and passive PoE plus four SFP fiber cages.
notes:
Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page specification table (https://mikrotik.com/product/crs112_8p_4s_in - 200, 364,485 B, read 2026-11-20), unless stated. 8x 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports, all 8 with PoE-out, 4x SFP ports (1G), 1x RJ45 serial console, "Max power consumption 160 W", "Max power consumption without attachments 10 W", IP20 desktop case.

WHAT WAS WRONG - the port census was right but nothing said how much the eight PSE ports can supply: no `poe` block, so `computePoe()` skipped the box at `if (!dev.poeBudget) continue;` and `show power inline` printed no budget for a switch whose model name is the PoE. The `poe` block now records the vendor's current limits and marks the budget unknown - the printed numbers are amperes that scale with the 18-28 V or 48-57 V input, and turning them into a single wattage would invent a figure MikroTik does not publish. The row also carried no source URL at all; it now cites the product page it was read from.

NOT MODELLED - no passive 24 V class (the page prints 802.3af/at only, though the same current limits apply at low voltage) and no 802.3bt.

poe.note: MikroTik prints current limits, never a watt ceiling: "PoE-out ports Ether1-Ether8", "PoE out 802.3af/at", "Low voltage PoE-Out current limit 1 A", "High voltage PoE-Out current limit 450 mA", "Max total out (A) 2.8A (18V-28V) & 1.4A (48V-57V)". Watts therefore follow the applied input voltage, so the budget is marked unknown rather than multiplied out.
